title: [Chapitre] III. Réseaux via découpages : notes manuscrites (08/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Chapter III, 'Réseaux via découpages', builds 'réseaux' (line or arrangement-like configurations) from cuttings. On the previous page, for a 3-element subset J={a,b,c} of a 'tranche' L, Grothendieck takes for each 2-element subset ε the component X_ε of the complement C(ε) that contains the third point. He then recovers the middle point b intrinsically: b is the point whose two pairs give disjoint components. This step uses density.

This page steps back to axiomatize the notion of 'tranche' (the machine transcription reads 'Thomson'; the handwriting says 'tranche'). He looks for a full subcategory C of ordered sets whose objects satisfy:
(a) L is directed upward and downward (filtrant croissant et décroissant) and has cardinality ≠ 1, so at least 2.
(b) Density: if x<y in L, there is z with x<z<y.
(c) If x∈L and L_{>x} is nonempty, then L_{>x} is again in C.
(c') The dual statement for L_{<x}.

He asserts that there is a largest such C, that it is stable under passing to the opposite order, and calls its objects tranches. A largest C exists because (a) and (b) are conditions on single objects, while (c) and (c') are closure conditions. The union of all classes satisfying them therefore satisfies them too: a greatest fixed point, or coinductive definition. Stability under opposite follows because the class of opposites of objects of C also satisfies the conditions, so it is contained in C.

Concretely, applying (c) and (c') iteratively shows that L is a tranche iff L itself, every nonempty open ray L_{>x}, L_{<x}, and every open interval ]x,y[ are directed both ways, dense and of cardinality ≥ 2. For totally ordered L this is simply: a dense linear order with at least 2 elements. Endpoints are allowed, which is consistent with p.17, where L_{≤a} 'with a not the smallest element' appears.

Remark (2) is a programme note. One should state explicitly which axioms a ternary relation R(a,b,c) must satisfy to define a 'tranche bi-ordonnée', i.e. a tranche structure up to reversal of the order, i.e. a betweenness relation. Likewise one should axiomatize the data of Soc P_2(L) (pairs of points) together with the relations R_ε (ε ∈ S_0) coming from the components C(ε). In other words: axiomatize the 'cutting' data from which the order is reconstructed.
errors: As written ('ens. ordonnés', in the Bourbaki sense of partially ordered sets), the conditions do not force total order. For example, Q×Q with the product order is directed both ways, dense, and its strict up-sets are again of the same kind, so it would be a 'tranche'. Totality is presumably intended, since all later usage (intervals, components of complements, sous-tranches) is linear. Either the ambient category should be totally ordered sets, or the conditions are insufficient.

For total orders, the directedness clause in (a) is automatic. The cardinality-≠1 clause is the substantive part; it also excludes the empty set only if 'filtrant' entails non-empty, which is the standard convention.

ideas.what: Defining 'tranche' as the largest full subcategory of ordered sets closed under passing to open rays and satisfying directedness, density and cardinality ≥2 (a coinductive / greatest-fixed-point definition)
ideas.modern_name: dense linear orders (with possible endpoints); coinductive definition of a class
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dense linear orders: Cantor (1895). Coinductive definitions are standard in logic and computer science.

ideas.what: Axiomatizing order-up-to-reversal by a ternary relation R(a,b,c)
Recovering the betweenness/order from components of complements of 2-point subsets (data Soc P_2(L), R_ε, C(ε))
ideas.modern_name: order reconstruction from separation/cutting data; separation relations for cyclic orders
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Huntington, Pasch-type axioms); also used in order-topology characterizations of R

missed.claim: Programme to axiomatize the 'tranche bi-ordonnée' through the relation R(a,b,c) and through the cutting data (Soc P_2(L), R_ε, C(ε)), presumably as groundwork for combinatorial 'réseaux'. This page only states the task; the classical answer (betweenness axioms) exists, so nothing substantively new is visible here.
missed.quote: Il faudrait expliciter quelle condition la relation R(a,b,c) doit satisfaire, pour définir une structure de tranche bi-ordonnée
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It documents how Grothendieck's 1986 'réseaux' work was founded on purely order-theoretic cutting data, of possible interest to historians of his late combinatorial/topological projects.

deep.surprise_reason: Elementary order theory: a coinductive characterization of dense linear orders plus a note to axiomatize betweenness. These are classical, and the page contains no new result. Its only interest is as a foundational detail of the little-known 'Réseaux via découpages' project.
transcription_corrections: 'Sur la notion de Thomson' should read 'Sur la notion de tranche'.
'Les objets de C sont les Thomson ordonnés' should be roughly 'Les objets de C sont les [appelés] tranches ordonnées'.
'structure de Thomson bi-ordonnée' should read 'structure de tranche bi-ordonnée' (or 'biordonnée').
In (a), 'non vide' is struck out and replaced by 'de cardinal ≠1 (donc ≥2)'; this is correctly captured.
'issues des C(ε)' is uncertain; it may read 'issues de' / 'ou bien les C(ε)'.
